newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends broadly lower on USDA data, funds.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends broadly lower on USDA data, funds.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled broadly lower in heavy volume on a combination of bearish USDA data, fund-related selling and seasonal harvest pressure, traders said.

KCBT wheat opened weak after USDA released wheat production figures that came in higher than analysts' estimates, traders said. In its June crop report, USDA estimated 1997-98 U.S. HRW wheat production at 921 million bushels, above analysts' average expectation of 899 million.
But wheat was hit further at midsession as funds chose to liquidate the July contract.
Traders said Benson-Quinn sold six million July bushels during the session and Refco sold four million July and three million September.
Losses were compounded by expectations that harvesting will gather steam this weekend in the southern U.S. Plains.
KCBT wheat settled five to 11 cents lower, with July down 11 cents at $3.76-1/2 per bushel.
Other featured players included Cargill Investor Services and FIMAT Futures, which each bought at least 2.5 million July bushels.
